name: Monaco

findings.local_actor: Monaco Telecom (sole licensed operator, state part-owned concession)
findings.summary: Monaco Telecom, the principality's only mobile operator, launched nationwide 5G in July 2019 using Huawei equipment for all network elements, under a 2018 agreement signed in Beijing and welcomed by the government.

sources.publisher: CMS Expert Guide to 5G Regulation and Law

findings.analyst_inference: Tier 5: commercial nationwide service. Government release undated on page; appears to be Sept 2018 signing. CMS guide (Mar 2025) still describes the Huawei partnership and notes no high-risk-vendor rules, and no swap was found, but no source confirms the vendor as of the run date, so still_current left null. Partnership dates to 2012, so 4G likely also Huawei (unverified).

findings.local_actor: Monaco Cloud (state-majority company with Monaco Digital as industrial shareholder)
findings.summary: The government chose AWS in 2019 to supply a hybrid sovereign cloud for e-government and business; state-majority Monaco Cloud launched it on AWS technology in September 2021, hosted in data centres inside Monaco with Luxembourg e-embassy backup.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole us under the equipment/stack rule: AWS supplies the cloud technology and updates, though ownership and data residency are Monegasque. Exact AWS product (e.g. Outposts) not stated in any opened source. Tier 5 as operational national government cloud; still_current from April 2026 reporting. Confidence medium because user/workload scale is not documented. Global cloud-region layer may not capture this on-premises arrangement.

findings.local_actor: Gouvernement Princier / Direction de la Surete Publique
findings.summary: German vendor Dallmeier designed and integrated Monaco's city-wide IP video surveillance system from a 2005 contract: about 520 cameras, police control-room recording and management software, later adding number-plate recognition on 30 traffic lanes.
findings.analyst_inference: Source reads as a Dallmeier case study relayed by trade press, so treated as S4. Pre-2020: Monaco Tribune (May and Dec 2023) reports 1,057 cameras but names no vendor, so the current vendor is unconfirmed and still_current null. A 2023 draft bill (No. 1087) would allow facial recognition; no vendor named.

facilities.null_reason: two searches found only Monaco Cloud's in-country data centres (coded under cloud) and a small Monaco Telecom basement data centre (DCD tag listing, Feb 2024); no AI campus or large foreign-controlled facility

silicon.null_reason: no dedicated search; no accelerator purchases surfaced at this scale

models.null_reason: two searches on government AI found policy statements and a sovereignty push but no named model-provider partnership or national model

research_gaps: Is Monaco Telecom's 5G (and 5G SA core, reportedly being integrated per CMS 2025) still Huawei-supplied as of 2026, and is any vendor swap planned given EU 5G Toolbox pressure via France?
Who currently supplies Monaco's 1,057-camera public video-protection system and any facial-recognition software following draft bill No. 1087 (Dec 2023)? Was it enacted?
Which AWS product underlies Monaco Cloud (e.g. Outposts or dedicated local zone), and does AWS retain operational access?
Does the Monaco government use any frontier model provider (e.g. via Monaco Cloud) for e-government services?
